sections.heading: Before or After Your Delivery Order

blocks.html: Roselle, NJ, carries its history lightly but wears it proudly. The borough that put electric light on the map in 1883 has grown into a diverse, community-minded place with a dining scene that reflects its cultural depth, parks that give residents genuine breathing room, and a Chestnut Street corridor that anchors daily life from one end to the other. For weed delivery Roselle residents rely on, Lady L keeps quality cannabis ready whenever you are, whether you're home along Linden Road, near the St. George's Avenue corridor, or anywhere in between.

blocks.title: Warinanco Park
blocks.html: Warinanco Park is one of Union County's most fully equipped public parks, spanning hundreds of acres across Roselle and Elizabeth with a recreational offering that covers nearly every outdoor activity imaginable. Baseball, basketball, cricket, fishing, handball, horseshoes, soccer, softball, and tennis sit alongside a bicycle path, running track, fitness trail, shuffleboard courts, picnic areas, and pedal boats on the park's central lake. An indoor ice skating rink with Wi-Fi access rounds out a facility that draws consistent use in every season.

blocks.title: Pinho's Bakery & Deli
blocks.html: Pinho's on Chestnut Street has been a Roselle institution since it opened, baking fresh bread, pastries, eclairs, napoleons, mousse tarts, cannolis, and layer cakes daily from the early hours of the morning. The deli side of the operation kicks in just as early, with breakfast sandwiches and grill platters starting at 5 AM followed by made-to-order subs on fresh-baked bread, Boar's Head cold cuts, housemade salads, and daily soups at lunch. Custom wedding and specialty cakes round out an operation that has built its reputation one honest, fresh product at a time.

blocks.title: La Llorona Street Mexican Kitchen & Tequila Lounge
blocks.html: La Llorona on Linden Road brings a vibrant Mexican street-food concept to Roselle, with a tequila lounge that adds an elevated social dimension to the experience. The kitchen draws on authentic Mexican recipes and bold flavors, with a full food menu running alongside an extensive tequila and cocktail program. Late-night hours on weekends make it one of the more distinctive destinations on the local dining scene.

blocks.title: Kokuyo Cocktail Bar
blocks.html: Kokuyo at 1135 Chestnut Street describes itself as a neighborhood third place, and the vibe backs that up. Island-inspired small plates, creative seasonal craft cocktails, and a relaxed, breezy atmosphere define the experience, with Golden Hour specials running daily from Wednesday through Sunday and all day on Sundays. Private event bookings are available for groups seeking a more intimate, curated experience than a typical bar night out.

blocks.title: Roselle Memorial Library
blocks.html: The Roselle Memorial Library at 104 West Fourth Avenue is one of the more full-featured public libraries in the area for a borough of its size. Services span digital borrowing via Libby, Hoopla, and Freegal Music; passport processing; notary services; ESL classes; municipal identification cards; computer and printing access; research databases; and reservable study rooms. A rotating calendar of community programming, including financial empowerment workshops, cultural celebrations, and adult education classes, reflects how deeply embedded the library is in the life of the borough.

blocks.title: Arminio Field Fitness Court
blocks.html: Arminio Athletic Field on Chestnut Street between Eighth and Ninth Avenues is a local landmark built through a collaboration between the Borough of Roselle and the public school district. The complex features a full football field and running track, a field house with a weight room, lockers, and meeting space, an outdoor NationalFit Fitness Court open to the public, and a Walk of Fame honoring former Roselle Ram football players. It's the kind of facility that gives residents a reason to show up and a reason to stay.

items.q: What age do you need to be for cannabis delivery in Roselle?
items.a_html: Per New Jersey's adult-use cannabis law, the minimum age is 21, and every Lady L delivery order adheres to that rule without exception. Your age is verified when you first register your Lady L account, and your driver will confirm your ID upon arrival before the handoff.

items.q: What ID does Lady L accept?

You’ll upload your ID to your Lady L account before placing your first order, and keep the physical document on hand when your driver arrives.

items.q: Is a medical cannabis card required to place a Roselle delivery order?
items.a_html: No medical card is necessary. Lady L operates as a fully adult-use cannabis microdispensary, which means the process is open to any customer 21 or older with a valid ID and a confirmed account. Nothing else is required.

items.q: What are the purchase limits for cannabis delivery orders?
items.a_html:
New Jersey caps each transaction at one ounce, or 28.35 grams, of usable cannabis across all product types combined. Here's how that breaks down:

  • Dried Flower/Bud: 28.35 grams (1 ounce).
  • Concentrates/Resin/Oils: 4 grams (solid or liquid/vaporized oil).
  • Ingestible Items (Gummies/Edibles): 1,000 mg of THC (roughly ten 100mg packages).
  • Maximum Possession Limit: Up to 6 ounces of cannabis and cannabis products.
  • Mixing Products: You can mix and match, for example, by purchasing 1/2 ounce of flower and 2 grams of concentrates.
  • Daily Limits: The 1-ounce limit is generally considered a daily limit across all dispensaries.

items.q: What taxes apply to Roselle weed delivery orders?
items.a_html: There are three taxes that apply to New Jersey adult-use cannabis: a 6.625% state sales tax, a $2.50-perounce Social Equity Excise Fee (SEEF), and a 2% municipal transfer or user tax in municipalities that have authorized it. All applicable charges appear at checkout, so there’s full transparency about what you’re paying for.
